assumptions: Source derivation: linear superposition of two stable sinusoidal acoustic components of equal amplitude at one observation point.
Application profile required by assignment: the frequencies are explicitly ordered f_hi>=f_lo; the full unordered absolute-value law is not executable here.
Source interpretation: beat rate counts amplitude maxima, not the sign-change rate of a signed modulation factor.

gaps: Add acoustic_beat_frequency and wave_frequency meanings; Hz supported. A caller must supply ordered carrier inputs or use an explicitly separately supported sorting adapter; no abs operator is assumed.

models.inverse_notes: Solve f_hi=f_b+f_lo given f_b>=0,f_lo>0: unique and satisfies ordering. Solve f_lo=f_hi-f_b given f_hi>0,0<=f_b<f_hi: unique positive lower carrier. Check f_b=2,f_lo=440 -> f_hi=442 and forward gives 2; inverse lower from 442 and 2 gives 440. f_b=0 uniquely implies equal carriers if either one is known; without either carrier, infinitely many common positive frequencies yield zero beating. No denominator exclusions in these affine inverse directions. The unordered inverse would have +/- branches; those are deliberately not claimed in this one-sided profile.
limitations: Audible slow beats require sufficiently close frequencies and a perceptual model; no quantitative audibility range or perceived pitch claim is made.
Unequal amplitudes, many components and frequency drift are not included in the inspected equal-amplitude derivation.
Equal frequencies give a time-independent resultant amplitude (possibly zero depending on phase), not a repeating perceptual beat at carrier frequency.

references.method: Independent synthetic phase-count oracle: over 0.5 s the components complete 221 and 220 cycles. Their relative phase advances exactly one cycle, so identical reinforcement repeats once every 0.5 s, or twice per second. This checks the important full-difference versus half-difference factor without evaluating the serialized subtraction. It is ideal kinematic evidence, not an auditory experiment. Decimal-rounding allowance only.

Limiting identity: equal carrier frequencies have constant relative phase, so no amplitude beat modulation repeats. Expected rate zero does not assert the carrier stops oscillating; source tuning discussion supports this limit.

rejection_cases.reason: A zero lower input is not one of the two oscillating positive-frequency acoustic carriers defined here.
Both ordered acoustic carrier frequencies are required.

relationship.locator: University Physics 1 Eq. 17.17, ordered-frequency application profile
relationship.translation_notes: Introduce f_hi=max of the two named source frequencies and f_lo=min, with ordering supplied/validated at the interface rather than computed by unsupported min/max/abs operators. The declared one-sided profile gives exact f_b=f_hi-f_lo; it is not an approximate replacement for absolute value. Hz-Hz=Hz (T^-1). The amplitude-envelope signed cosine has half the frequency difference, but positive beat maxima repeat twice per envelope-sign cycle, so beat rate is the full difference. Equality is admitted as zero beating, not a zero-frequency carrier. This is the assignment's expressly permitted one-sided acoustic beat case, not optical interference curation.

sources.evidence: The beat rate is the magnitude of the frequency difference. With explicitly ordered higher/lower inputs the magnitude is exactly the nonnegative difference; equal frequencies remove temporal beating. The source's widely separated tuning-fork example is not used as an auditory-beat validation.

assumptions: Source boundary condition: light passes from vacuum to a material while frequency remains unchanged.

Application profile making the source statement precise: stationary medium/interface in one time frame; linear time-invariant elastic transmission, no frequency conversion and a nonzero transmitted mode.

gaps: Reuse proposed wave_frequency for both ports with distinct incident/transmitted mode contexts and an explicit common interface/frame relation. Hz supported. Requires mode/context binding capability and scientific conditions; not automatic global equality of same-unit frequencies.

models.inverse_notes: Inverse f_i=f_t is unique for f_t>0 only when the same stationary elastic boundary/mode pairing is already identified. Example f_t=6e14 Hz restores f_i=6e14 and the forward identity. Zero is outside the oscillating-mode domain; this equation does not determine material refractive index or interface motion. Frequency agreement alone is not evidence that two independently observed waves are a compatible incident/transmitted pair.
limitations: Moving interfaces/media, nonlinear conversion, inelastic scattering and time-varying boundaries do not follow this identity.
Does not specify transmission amplitude, direction, wavelength, index or energy transport.
The two ports represent different physical mode instances; matching the unit Hz alone is insufficient to assert this boundary relation.

references.method: Independent synthetic phase timing: the same interface field repeats after 2e-15 s; in stationary linear transmission the outgoing boundary field has that same repeat interval, so it supplies 5e14 cycles/s. Expected is the independently counted boundary repetition rate, not a reported experiment. 1 Hz tolerance is solely floating-point allowance on an optical-scale exact synthetic frequency, not a physical uncertainty.

A second synthetic boundary clock has 600 complete cycles per 1e-12 s at both sides of the same stationary linear boundary, hence 6e14 Hz. Counting shared boundary cycles independently of speed/wavelength demonstrates that a changed refractive index is not a frequency scaling factor. Floating-point allowance only.

assumptions: Source definition: paraxial effective focal length and paraxial entrance pupil at infinite conjugates.
Application profile: positive converging imaging system; real-is-positive focal convention and one specified wavelength/lens setting.
Source distinction: entrance pupil is viewed from object space; conventional f-number differs from finite-conjugate working f-number.

gaps: Add f_number and entrance_pupil_diameter; reuse focal_length only with the correct effective-focal-length/reference-plane definition. m and 1 supported. A back focal distance or glass outer diameter is not an automatic compatible binding.

models.inverse_notes: Solve f=N_f*D_ep given N_f>0,D_ep>0, or D_ep=f/N_f given f>0,N_f>0; each gives one positive root and retains infinite-conjugate EFL/pupil context. Check N_f=3,D_ep=0.04 -> f=0.12 and forward returns 3. N_f=4,f=0.1 -> D_ep=0.025 and forward gives 4. N_f=0 has no positive finite-f, positive-diameter solution; D_ep=0 is an infinite-f-number limit, not a zero f-number. No inverse identifies mechanical iris size without the stop/pupil imaging relation.
limitations: Does not calculate exposure, transmitted light, diffraction resolution, numerical aperture or depth of field.
Finite-conjugate working f-number needs pupil-magnification/conjugate conditions; do not reuse a signed transverse m in a magnitude-only correction without evidence.
A fully closed zero-diameter pupil has no finite conventional f-number in this serialization.

references.method: Published Ansys design specifies F/4 and 100 mm EFL and explicitly calculates 25 mm EPD; preserve stated F/4 as expected 4. Normalize mm to m. These are nominal design constraints, not measured calibration values; tolerance only permits floating-point arithmetic on the exact stated design.

references.method: Published Edmund Table 1 row f/4 for the nominal 25 mm singlet lists rounded diameter 6.3 mm. Preserve expected f-number 4; nominal data produce 3.968253968. A diameter rounded to 0.1 mm allows 6.25-6.35 mm; at the lower edge the f-number reaches 4. The nominal-to-edge difference 0.0317461 is bounded by 0.033. This input-rounding propagation, not an arbitrary enlarged output tolerance, explains the mismatch.

Independent exact synthetic geometric count: three 40 mm entrance-pupil diameters span the 120 mm effective focal distance, so the system is f/3. This checks both metre normalization and a non-4 ratio without claiming an empirical lens. Floating-point allowance only.

rejection_cases.reason: A closed zero-diameter entrance pupil gives no finite defining ratio or finite through-aperture imaging configuration.
